Skip ghost notes with `--min-velocity`, play MIDIs that rely on BASSMIDI's very short notes, and DX12 works.

## Before you upgrade

- **Some command-line options moved to dev mode.** The engine's tuning and debugging options, such as `--steal`, `--admit`, `--no-lfo`, `--no-mod-env`, `--block-csv`, `--layers`, `--lookahead-ms` and `--limiter-release-ms`, and the `null` command are no longer in the downloads. A script that uses one now stops with "unexpected argument". `render --help` lists what's left. If you need them, build Kestrel yourself with `--features dev`; the README explains how.

## What's new

- **`--min-velocity N`.** Skips every note quieter than velocity N before it reaches the GPU. On black MIDI full of ghost notes, that can make a render many times faster. In the guided renderer, type it at the last step.
- **`--note-grid`.** Holds notes to BASSMIDI's 4 ms envelope grid, so very short notes still sound. Some MIDIs, such as ones that encode audio as one-sample notes, render silent without it. Off by default.
- **Dev mode for self-builds.** `cargo build --release --features dev` keeps the developer options.
- **Fewer SFZ warnings.** The CC range and crossfade opcodes (`loccN`, `hiccN`, `xfin_loccN` and the like) are now ignored quietly.
- **For GUI builders.** The API's `ready` line now says whether it's a `release` or `dev` build. See [API.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/API.md).

## Fixes

- **`--gpu-backend dx12` works.** It used to fail after a minute with a shader error. The Windows download is bigger now, because it carries the shader compiler that fixes this.

**A note for Windows users:** DX12 might sound like the natural choice on Windows, but Vulkan renders noticeably faster in our tests, so Kestrel keeps Vulkan as the default. Only switch to DX12 if Vulkan doesn't work on your machine.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.1.2-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.1.2-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.1.2-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

The macOS and Linux builds haven't been tested yet. If you try one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
